newsitem.title: CHINA: China welcomes Iraq's oil-for-food deal with U.N.
newsitem.headline: China welcomes Iraq's oil-for-food deal with U.N.

text.p: China on Tuesday welcomed Iraq's acceptance of terms set by the United Nations under an oil-for-food deal, saying it would contribute to peace and stability in the Gulf.

"We welcome this," Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai said of Iraq accepting last month U.N. terms for the partial flow of its crude oil to world markets after a six-year blockade under a U.N. embargo imposed for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

"We hope this resolution could be smoothly implemented to ease the suffering of the Iraqis due to sanctions," Cui told a news briefing. "(This) is conducive to restoring peace and stability in the Gulf region at an early date."
The oil-for-food deal signed in May provides for oil exports worth $2 billion every six months to enable Iraq buy food and medicine.
The overall curbs on Baghdad's oil exports are tied to its coming clean about its weapons of mass destruction.
The United Nations launched an appeal in September for millions of dollars to meet the urgent needs of more than two million destitute and internally displaced Iraqis.
